title: Constructibility of finite pushforward of an open quotient constant
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, ℓ a natural number such that R = Λ/(ℓ) is finite as a set, X a Noetherian scheme, ν:Y→X a finite morphism, and j:U→Y an open immersion. Then ν_*j_! of the constant Λ-module sheaf R on U is constructible [def-constructible-constructible], using direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero].

source.place: Proof sketch: cokernel constructibility and vanishing over the isomorphism locus; arbitrary-mono generalization justified by finite stalks

proof.text: Y is Noetherian since it is finite over X. The constant quotient module sheaf is finite locally constant since Λ/(ℓ) is cyclic. Extension by zero along the quasi-compact open immersion preserves constructibility.

Apply finite pushforward constructibility to the underlying finite abelian sheaf. The resulting sheaf remains killed by ℓ. Its module operations factor through the finite ring R, so on each finite-set constant stratum a refinement trivializes the finitely many R-operations. The resulting finite constant R-modules are finitely generated over Λ. This yields the required constructible module sheaf; no Noetherian ring assumption on Λ is used.
